A.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: one opaque portrait 1024x1536 production overhead background tile for chapter TWO "Lost City" of an aircraft shooter.
The supplied first-chapter harbor painting is STYLE REFERENCE ONLY for clean readable material planes and dimensional hand-painted lighting. The new subject is a unified MODERN CITY street, with no sea, docks, rocky banks, island platforms or medieval arches.
Rebuild the entire scene as ONE coherent aerial environment painting with physically consistent ground and building volumes. NOT a collection of separate isometric house assets on a blank road. Not an asset sheet, diorama, paper cutout, sticker, toy city or vector illustration. Use a single high overhead orthographic camera with modest visible facades; every building, courtyard, tree, curb, road mark and shadow shares the same camera, scale and ground plane.
Main depth requirement: a clear believable sunlight direction FROM THE UPPER RIGHT casts soft-but-defined building shadows TOWARD THE LOWER LEFT. In particular, buildings on the RIGHT must cast broad grounded shadows across their forecourts and ONTO THE ASPHALT STREET, overlapping paving seams and faded road paint, proving the buildings rise from that same surface. Shadows are anchored directly to building footprints, with continuous wall-foot contact and no detached halo. Tree canopies cast smaller coherent shadows onto paving and asphalt in the same direction. Roofs catch warm light; blue-gray shaded facade planes remain readable. Shadows must not be absent, random, outlined rings, or a dark stripe traced around each block. Do not paint every face equally bright.
Street, pedestrian paving and recessed courtyards are continuous material regions of a large uninterrupted city ground plane. Thin low curbs and multiple flush driveway cuts connect them. Break the closed cutout silhouette with interlocking asphalt repairs, paving transitions and connected small side-road mouths. Some buildings partly occlude ground markings and one subdued crosswalk ties the street sides together. No bright perimeter outline, extruded pavement skirt, isolated polygon platform, surrounding moat or hard cutout edge.
Modern ordinary architecture: rectangular windows, flat roofs, credible reinforced-concrete floor slabs and steel/AC details. Different footprints, heights, setbacks and building orientations, not two repeated bookend rows of identical facades all facing the same angle. Buildings are integrated into continuous outer city lots extending off the frame; use an asymmetrical side alley and connected yard to make a believable urban block. Keep some visible ruin corners and a limited exposed floor, but clean surviving surfaces. Match the reference's broad painted forms and controlled detail. No brown dirt wash, all-over grunge, dense microcracks or noisy weathering. Restrained healthy olive/teal plants in a few deliberate clumps.
Road is desaturated slate blue-gray asphalt, not a uniformly flat dark backdrop. Give it large subtle coherent light/shadow shapes, a few faint patches/fissures and quiet worn road paint. It connects naturally to the same shadowed ground under buildings. Keep a continuous quiet flight route within the middle 40%; no huge rubble blockage, high-contrast zebra pattern or bright patch under the player. Overall readability at phone size matters.
SCROLL CONNECTION DESIGN: the top and bottom 10% are low, open cross-street/paved transition ground with no tall building, roof, wall or long shadow cut by the image edge. All large buildings stop short of those bands. The central road opening is centered; endpoint tones are quiet slate asphalt so the companion tiles can meet without slicing architecture. Keep interest inside the middle 80%, with natural irregular street width and asymmetry rather than an empty straight runway.
No clouds, fog, aircraft, humans, enemies, vehicles, bullets, pickup symbols, UI, readable signs, text, logos, watermark or alpha transparency. Output ONE finished full-frame background, not before/after or multiple panels.
Segment A: a believable abandoned mixed residential/service block. A modest apartment shell and connected shaded service alley occupy one outer side, with a lower commercial/maintenance building and a recessed yard on the other. A large right-side building shadow must visibly cross onto the road toward lower left. Preserve depth and unified daylight over decorative detail.
